# <mark class="story">The Story so Far</mark>

<mark class="music">♫    -     ▸     4.1.1 Time Stretched Thin Like a Web      ↻¹</mark>

Pelotharna, a sunken city built on the bones of another.  
Eternis, a kingdom that disappeared.
The Megadome, a cocoon that never cracked.

Your adventures have taken you all across the surface of the Dragon’s Garden, and that is to say nothing of your treks through other planes, and the pockets between them.

You’ve saved a city overrun by a new breed of monstrosities. You’ve come face to face with a broken overseer, trapped in a divine prison. And you have subdued the heart of a new evil, in the hopes that your efforts might bring stability to the Silver City. A kingdom-sized meteor, teetering on the edge of a cloud.

It hasn’t been easy. It hasn’t been simple. And it hasn’t been clean.

In the last several hours alone, you've had to fight your way through the twisted, cackling mind of a demigod. You have become bound to each other through horrors that ordinary folks have no concept of. But you do. Because *you* do not have the luxury of ignorance. You've been asked to shoulder divine threats, choose between imperfect solutions, and face down the limits of your own mortality.

You are the Misfortune’s Misfits. A quilt woven of hope, tragedy, and gritted teeth. Has fate appointed you its champion? Or its jester? Moment to moment, her motives elude you.

All you know is that now, right now in this moment, you are falling.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Battle After Battle      ↻¹</mark>

You fall, and Belbe’s taunts echo through your head: “Do you wonder, who will the son of madness become next? Perhaps the little friends will stow the son of madness away somewhere safe. Somewhere far away from all the other tiny sprouts in the garden? But how long do the little friends imagine they could keep the son hidden? See you soon, little friends.”

Were these the ravings of a lunatic or the prophecy of a god? You were given no time to contend with this question as hundreds of tar-black wings sprouted from Belbe's seraphim form - closing around her, hardening - cocooning into an obsidian egg, with feathery reliefs.

Then, a vision took you. Or perhaps it was a conscious experience… Your sanity has been too frayed to distinguish one from the other. A dragonborn man draped in court jester’s clothes. He clapped and jingled and laughed at a spinning toy top, knocking it off balance with a sickly “topsy turvy!”

Now, in the sanctum of the lambs, gravity no longer has meaning. The ground beneath you might as well be the ceiling, or the walls. You’re caught somewhere between falling and floating, the city hitching and screeching against the failing chains of Marduun’s artifact. Cries of terror from the festival above overwrite every quiet moment.

You’ve done your part. You’ve subdued Belbe. And Valenthe has done hers. The machine has transposed the egg.

Now, Timar must do his part, if the Silver City is to survive. You’ve begged. You’ve pleaded with him. You appealed to whatever reason his fractured mind still holds. But he’s barely moved, barely bothered to even look up. He is free of the crypt, but his eyes are dim, and he doesn't believe it.

This is where we continue our story, with the rings of the city, the slums below, and perhaps all of De Drakengardt, at the mercy of an overseer whose mind was broken centuries ago.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Featherfall      ↻¹</mark>

However. Celeste. Your mind is elsewhere.

# <mark class="story">The Picnic</mark>

> [!quote]+ Exander
> “Celeste? Celeste?” The words land soft on your ears. The voice is familiar, sweet. It’s your father’s voice.

You find yourself sitting on the ground, legs to the side, back straight, shoulders back. Poised with dignity, just as you were taught. As all highborns have been taught. Dignity, while it is your birthright, must be maintained, or it will erode. Your mother's words repeat themselves often in your mind.

Your fingers brush the fabric beneath you. A picnic blanket. Laid out on the grass of a courtyard somewhere inside the inner ring of the city. Your lunch plates are scraped clean. Your intricate oxygen masks lay in the picnic basket. Here in the heart of Luna, the air is perfectly pressurized and filtered, one of the city's more recent innovations, but one that requires too much energy to cover an entire ring, let alone the whole city. And so the council ruled that these pockets of breathable air would be reserved to the courtyards of Luna, the capital ring. You and your father are the only two here in this courtyard.

> [!quote]+ Exander
> Are you still with me, little star? Or have you sailed off into the sky again?

A gentle breeze dances across the lush grass and up the leaves of the great oak in the courtyard’s center. The sun warms your back.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

> [!quote]+ Exander
>“Hey! It’s just us here today,” he says with a look of mischief, before kicking out his legs and sprawling out over the blanket in a particularly childish way.
>
>“Come on, loosen up a little. Your mother doesn’t have to know.”

> [!quote]+ Exander
>Rules are important, I suppose. But what’s the point of family if you can’t be yourself? I might as well be just another stuffed shirt.

> [!quote]+ Exander
> My little star, your mother carries a great deal on her shoulders. If she is harsh, perhaps it is a plea. Her own way of asking for our help. When *we* sit light on her shoulders, I think her whole world becomes easier to carry.
> 
Celeste, my little star, I have been thinking. This city sets its compass toward progress, toward innovations that shape the destiny of all. It is a lofty goal. But perhaps we neglect... I don't know… Sometimes I think perhaps our ambition eclipses our heart.”
>
“We speak of the lands below as if they are a savage people, but were we not all planted by the same gods and their gardeners?”

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⏸︎</mark>

> [!quote]+ Exander
> A garden bed grows both roses and weeds without discrimination. And a weed is only a weed because we gave it that name. I want you to remember that, Celeste. A weed is only a weed because *we* labeled it so.
# <mark class="story">City Falling</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇡  +  ⇥     4.1.1 Sky Over Tokyo      ↻¹</mark>

Shearing metal, tearing screeching shearing metal rattles your chest as the city *lurches* to a *violent* halt, *ripping* you away from the memory, or daydream, or whatever it is your mind was just doing.

Everyone make a strength saving throw. Celeste, if you are still on your broom, make a dexterity saving throw as the sudden stop threatens to send you into a collision with the ground below. \[DC 25, knocked prone\] 

Those who fail are knocked prone. The deafening scrape of metal against stone *rings* in your ears: Professor Marduun’s **Stratos Tether** finds purchase again, but the shearing groans tell you it won’t be for long. The Tether was always meant to be a contingency. But the chains are faltering against the magnitude of the city rings.

Timar lies before you like a stray dog in the gutter. Eyes closed, barely moving, as if he's crushed under the full weight of the seven moons.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

Timar blinks. His eyes study yours. They flick between your faces, trying to make sense of where he is, or who you are, of what this is.

The chains outside the city crack, and unceremoniously, you’re thrown into a free fall.
# <mark class="story">Time Slowing</mark>
However, Skrimhawk. This moment slows for you.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⏸︎</mark>

Here and there, light begins pouring through little cracks in the air. It's peaceful. It reminds you of the times you used to stare off the dock at rays of sunlight, watching them meander across the ocean floor. Only now, they sway in the stale air around you. A thousand fragile traces of light rippling and dancing lazily through the sanctum. They aren't dull, but they aren’t very bright either. They’re just blurry little veins, casually finding their way to nowhere in particular.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇡  +  ⇥     4.1.1 Wending      ↻¹</mark>

It's in this moment you realize, time is at a standstill, but only for you. Nothing moves but you and the ripples of light. A quick glance across the frozen faces of your fellow party members, and you see their focus is on Timar, their weapons. But no one else is moving and no one else seems to have slipped outside of time, like you have in this moment.

A voice.

> [!quote] Chronos
>- *Chuckle*; *we’re* in quite a pickle, hm? Would you say no to some help?
>- Who I am may just be the wrong question for a moment like this, hm?

> [!quote] Chronos
You may call me Chronos... As long as you remember that Chronos is not my real name.
>
What can I tell you about myself? Ah! I once served the Overseer of time with undying fealty. And I know the *rivers* of time better than most.
>
Why am I talking to you? Ah, yes, well... You have caught the eye of Cemus, I'm sure you know that. Did you think there would not be others?
>
Barduk Faremeadow, you carry a great artifact in your pocket like a trinket. It will take more than a locket and a few keys exchanged between friends to ensure its safety. It’s a wonder you haven’t been hunted down already, but that’s a discussion for another… *time*. *chuckle*

At this, the arcane multilock finds its way out of the bag of holding, floating easy. One by one, the locks click open, echoing across the stillness around you. The lid creaks open on its hinges, unhurried. The container falls away gradually, leaving the Chronogual Staff hovering in its place. The Orb’s turbulent cerulean waters churn a little faster and glow a little brighter each time Chronos speaks:

> [!quote] Chronos
I ask you for your trust. I appreciate the weight of such a request, in a moment like this. I wish I had introduced myself sooner. But Marduun does not typically fail. I had not accounted for that. Some fate we find ourselves in now, hm?
>
I promise you, I have my own reasons for holding my cards close. And I have my reasons for wanting to still see the sun tomorrow, next month, and the next several hundred years. Such a future seems rather unlikely if Timar is not shaken from his stupor, hm?
>
One nasty little issue to contend with. It’s already too late. Even if Timar were to suddenly come to his senses, right now, we are *inches* from impact. The fiery air enveloping the falling city has already begun to lick out at the slums below.
>
So then, why have I waited until this moment to begin our conversation, hm? If I’m to be honest, I was hoping you and your companions would have arrived at a solution that did not require my involvement. I have put myself in great danger by speaking so candidly, but I do not wish to see the whole of the dragon’s garden beneath a thick cloud of dust and ash. I believe we are aligned in this, hm?
>
Barduk, you have treated the flow of time with sanctity and respect. For this, you have both my admiration and gratitude. But we are out of options. Cemus abandoned his duties long ago. The gardeners have scattered. The gods are off building their new worlds. Timar is the only solution left. But he needs more time to come to himself.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Ice Gate      ↻¹</mark>

> [!quote] Chronos
\**Sigh*\*...This is the bit I was dreading. You must walk against the flow of time, and you must do it now. But you should know, such an act comes at a heavy cost to a mortal being. You may... not... Live through it. I cannot say with any certainty that... that you will survive.
>
I regret to frame things in such a way, but... I must ask. I must be certain. Barduk, would you prefer to die alongside your friends, or risk dying alone, if that's what it takes to save them?
>
Come, then. I will take your hand.

The staff now hovers right at your fingertips.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> Do you take it in your hand?

As you do, the blurry streaks of light that have been hovering around the sanctum begin to glow a bit brighter. Their light leaks outward, expanding until all that’s left is light. And the light flows around your feet. Around your one good ankle, around your false leg, trickling and babbling like a stream beneath you.

You look at your shadow, and it reveals to you something you don’t expect to see: chains run from your shadow's hands to six shackled silhouettes you recognize. Timar, then Celeste, Kiktal, Flicker, Spark, and HAL. You don’t see *them*, you see their shadows, all connected to the chain in your shadows grip. You *feel* the weight of these chains, and you *hear* their rattle. But you don't see them.

A swirl of cerulean rises from the pale waters.

> [!quote] Chronos
This way, Barduk! We must not dally here!

Chronos' voice comes from inside the swirl. He’s only 7 feet upstream.

You see the reflection of ages past in deep swells, and the reflection of the past 30 seconds in the shallow ripples at your ankles.

> [!quote] Chronos
Move slowly toward me, but... you must not linger. I feel Cemus’s eye turning toward us as we speak.
>
Be swift, but be delicate. The less ripples you create here, the better for us all.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup> as you take your first step forward, as you pull the six shadows behind you.

It feels like moving through primordial sludge. You muster all your might just to take a single step forward.

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.

You have **4** steps left.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup>

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.

You have **3** steps left.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup>

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.

You have **2** steps left.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup>

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.


<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Factorio Gathering      ↻¹</mark>

The **next step** will put you inside the swirl. This time, I need you to

>Make a **Charisma saving throw** <sup>(DC 40)</sup>

as pools of pale gray form in the peripherals of your vision, and that gray begins to swallow you. An eye opens across the distant horizon. Its eyelid: a nest of white feathers. Cemus, the Overseer of Time. His attention turns to you.

<hr class="short">

You push your head into the swirl, then your chest, then your legs; and each movement costs you something your body has never paid before. A flurry of cosmic force that saps from you and rips into you.

> [!success]- Critical
> You fight the pull into unconsciousness, and your resolve holds. The Eye of Cemus follows you, but you reject his gaze.
> 
> You push fully into the swirl, and you land soft in the sanctum once again.

> [!success]+
> You fight the pull into unconsciousness, and your resolve holds. But the Eye of Cemus pierces through you, and you take 204 points of psychic damage, halved to 102.
> 
> You push fully into the swirl, and you collapse in the sanctum once again.

> [!failure]+
> The gray continues to steal more and more of your vision, and your consciousness slips away from you. You take a level of exhaustion.
> 
> *If not dead:* you go unconscious, and your hit points are reduced to 0. You push fully into the swirl, and you collapse in the sanctum. You are dying.

The rest of you, back in the sanctum, feel a sensation of being lifted, slowly, and set back down, but it’s not a physical sensation. In fact, it’s very distinct from the physical chaos around you. *This…* This you feel in whatever part of you tracks the passage of time. You feel it passing through you, like a soft wave that hasn’t broken yet.


<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 We're All Monsters      ↻¹</mark>

Then, shearing screeches cut the softness. The chains of the wizard’s artifact, again catch the city. And you realize, you remember this moment. It was the last moment the city was still held in place. But you’re all living through it again. The last few seconds before the chains snapped; and before the city broke into it's final free fall.

This time, Timar’s eyes are already open. They're explore the room, flitting back to your faces, looking for clarity. Gradually, a sense of understanding begins to well up in Timar’s eyes. Then something clicks in place. He snaps his gaze up to the stained-glass mural above. His brow narrows.

He unfurls his wings, and darts upward with a gust that rattles the loose bits of stone beneath you and whips at the edges of your clothing.

And once again, the chains holding the city, break.

The air stills for a fraction of a second. Whatever screams of terror you previously heard from the city surface above, are now mute, or maybe your mind has muted them for you in a panic.

Timar charges toward the mural. He does not slow, instead wrapping his wings around himself as a cloak, a shield, bracing for impact against the thick stained glass.

Adrenaline, or whatever equivalent chemical you experience as a being, slows your reality to a crawl.

You are falling again. You know you are because everything up to this moment has told you so. Your feet left the ground some time ago. You feel weightless, but you know it’s a lie. One told told to you by your own mind, which has no anchor to define what falling even is anymore. 

Then, the sound of glass, shattering. Timar bursts through the mural, above the city’s surface, and flies out of view. A million tiny shards of stained glass fall like sheets of rain in a thunderstorm. Timar has left the sanctum.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Machinrium      ↻¹</mark>

Now…

You’ve all confronted death before. But this moment feels different. *Yes*, people die. But entire civilizations? Every face you’ve ever seen, every hand you’ve ever held, every name you’ve ever cursed, all, at risk of elimination—from the lands below, from history, from the mortal realm itself. This moment holds not just the possibility of death. It holds erasure. The second fall.

The gods haven’t intervened since the first age, the wizard’s chains failed, and all the strength and all the spell work you’ve accumulated up until now have no hope of catching a city-sized meteor.

All the fates of every last soul in the garden rest now on the wings of a broken demigod, newly released from an age-old hell.

There’s nothing now but waiting. Time passes and it does not. Eternities seem to fold themselves into seconds as you wait for whatever comes next.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⏸︎</mark>

And then… It’s subtle — the way the ground begins to close the distance between itself and your own feet. It moves toward you, carefully, gradually, until you gently land on your feet once again. Gravity is light but it's steadily growing stronger. Each passing moment confirms that you're standing on solid, still ground once again. 

The city slows to a quiet stillness.

Silence rings in your ears. It's just you now and your fellow party members, sitting in the heavy silence of the Sanctum.

Soft bits of moonlight stream in, cut against the jagged edge of the shattered mural above.

But the city is held. Timar holds The Silver City.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 The Void      ↻¹</mark>

> [!failure]+
>Skrimhawk lies motionless on the cold stone.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do now?

# <mark class="story">Comings and Goings</mark>
You are approached by a city official, some poor gnome who seems like he's in way over his head Punar Tillam. He addresses you, attempting to fulfill his civic duty and take some sort of action. In a shaky voice, he manages a meager:

> [!Quote] Punar Tillam
> What happened down here?

> [!Quote] Punar Tillam
> Follow me, please. There is a great shock in the streets, but I cannot lose you in the chaos.
 
 His voice is pleading, sincere. 

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⇥      4.1.1 Trio for Willa      ↻¹</mark>

The next moments are a blur.

As you come to the surface, you see wreckage. Many buildings… lie in *ruin*, toppled over by the jolting halts when the wizards chains failed. The peacekeepers do not move as they should. They hardly move at all. Dust covers the streets and stabs at your lungs.

The aftermath is a cold and heartless calm. Stunned citizens quietly cry and bleed and sit in a haze and look to the horizon. And you notice how much closer that horizon now sits. The city has fallen far from its proud heights.

Bodies lie still among the rubble. Some are attended to with wrappings and medical salves. Many are unconscious and perhaps many more are dead.

You glance beyond the city’s edge, where Timar stands on a cloudy perch, wings outstretched. The light of the moon and the stars refract through him like glittering waters. They form a soft halo at the edges his silhouette. It’s a majestic sight, but unrest twitches through him in erratic waves. Shivers that stab him, through his body, through his face. And each time, a hint of a tremor agitates the ground beneath your feet. But, the city holds.

Punar leads you to a room within the high court and tells you "wait here." But his words are half-command, half-plea, like he's unsure if he's overstepping his rank. He steps out of the room, and closes the door. There’s a constant shuffling of muffled footsteps in the hallway outside.

<hr class="short">

The hours bleed into each other. Council members and officials coming and going, all in a frantic rush, often asking you the same things as those that had questioned you before them.

Questions like “Who are you,” and “what were you doing below,” and “how did you infiltrate the city” and “aren’t you the exiled daughter of Professor Efthalia,” and “weren’t you banished on account of the red professor’s death?” These questions all spew out at you, soaked in suspicion, but no one really knows what to do with your answers. They just nod, jot down a note, and leave you alone again.

# <mark class="story">In a Quiet Room</mark>
But for now, it seems the activity has slowed, and the room you're in goes quiet.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Night      ↻¹</mark>

In the stillness of the room, you notice a pitcher of water sitting in the center of the long table before all of you. The water inside, sits at a slant. The cups set before each of you also filled with water that rests--ever so slightly--at that same slant.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> Now what? What do you do?

The room you're in is composed of warm tones and calm wood grains. No windows. There’s a painting on the wall opposite the door: a small raft floating on a sea of constellations, painted in deep purples and blues with a single silver sail.

> [!tip] Roleplay

Eventually, the door opens to a familiar face of red scales. The wizard that gave your efforts a fighting chance from the land, Professor Allao Marduun. He looks haggard. His hunched shoulders hang much deeper than usual.


> [!quote] Marduun
> - I have no words for the relief it is to see you breathing.
> - I have located your parents. They are battered, much like the rest of the city, but they are alive. Scraped up a bit, perhaps. But their fates… could have easily turned another way. Many were not so fortunate.

There’s a despondent look in his eyes.

> [!quote] Marduun
> I had to burn several ancient artifacts in order to hold the city as long as it held. But the chains gave way and I was left with nothing by my terror.

Celeste, Hal, you notice something, or rather the lack thereof. The candles at the end of his staff have melted, down to the wick. For the first time in all your years of knowing him, they no longer burn black. They no longer burn at all.

> [!quote] Marduun
> - I have convinced the powers that be not to imprison you, which is no small feat given your past conviction, my dear Celeste. However, it seems that for the time being, you are all caught in a state somewhere between captivity and freedom. They would not have you leave the halls of high court until they are able to find their footing, in a manner of speaking. They wish for you to remain here, and they are prepared to enforce their wish. I do apologize, you deserve a hero's welcome. But this was the best I could do.
> - It is a testament to the city’s ancestry that so many buildings survived.
> - Councilman Castiel Ralora was found in a bunker, a craven little cocoon he carved beneath the city surface for an occasion such as this. I happily report to you that he has been detained with his wrists cuffed. It did not take much convincing. Between the newly dislodged city, and the return of my living and breathing body, I believe there are now many ears ready to hear.
> - I suspect there are some houses among them that knew Ralora’s lie and kept it with their eyes wide open. But the wallpaper has torn from the walls, and now the termites have nowhere to flee. They will be found out.
> - "These are unprecedented times." Celeste, you’d expect to see a slight grin on his face, this is exactly the kind of thing he’d say through a grin. Marduun always enjoyed a good shake-up. But there's no grin to be found. Just a weary old man bowing under the weight of all the lives lost when his magic failed, and the chains snapped.
> - Come, I’ll show you to your accommodations in the halls.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.2 The Night's Accommodations</mark>

# <mark class="story">Accomodations</mark>

The old wizard leads you out the door, where a man—some mix of gnomish and elven—stands guard. For Celeste and Hal, it’s a sight you’ve never seen before--a man standing guard. People don’t stand guard. That’s what Peacekeepers are for. But as you walk down the grandiose corridors of the high court, you realize there are no peacekeepers anywhere, and there should be. Here of all places, there always are.

A staircase at the end of a hall leads several stories up, and you exit into another hall. Narrower. Lined with the kind of long, thin windows that start at the floor and end in a pointed arch far above eye level. Rays of moonlight filter in, lazy and blurred like plucked strings on a harp.

The city rings outside lie still. Some of you catch a glimpse of a clock in the hall. Dawn is only an hour away, at most.

Down the hall, a man is placed outside one of the rooms, standing guard. Marduun stops at his door. There's a plaque on it that reads “Solveris”.

Marduun opens the door with a creak, ignoring the man.

There are eight beds inside, stacked atop each other in pairs of two.

Celeste, HAL, it strikes you as a room that might have been built as lodging for the family of a visiting dignitary, back in ancient times when the city still did that sort of thing. Generations before your lifetime.

It's all immaculately maintained despite its disuse. There’s a desk, probably carved from some great ancient wood pillaged from some great ancient forest in the north. A few lounging chairs and a fainting couch encircle a coffee table, all tastefully scattered about.

> [!quote] Marduun
Rest. I shall make your case personally in… whatever remains of the city's court system. Although… it may take some time. An exiled infiltrator and her cohorts may not be the subject that requires the most immediate attention, given the state of affairs.
>
Sleep. I will find you when the time is right.

With that, he steps into the hall, and closes the door.

# <mark class="story">Nothing Left but Our Words</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Vovo e Vovo ↻¹</mark>

The days that followed felt as if they both dragged on *and* flew by, in the way that it can feel when you're trapped in a room and then passed around for questioning and then stuffed back into a room for safe keeping.

Eventually your testimony was requested in the high court. No trial was held against you. The evidence in your favor had mounted so completely that no trial was deemed necessary.

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir 
"You are free to go."

Councilwoman of Innovation Veldrin Illiir makes eye contact with each of you as she speaks. Cases like this are usually led by Councilman of Order Soaruun Hun’ath, but even from your sequestered quarters, you've heard rumors of his backroom deals with House Ralora.

Veldrin continues.

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir 
But I do hope you’ll stay and allow us to repay you, if such a debt can be repaid. Especially you, Ms. Efthalia. There are no words of regret sincere enough to make whole the injustice lodged against you. And yet it seems we have little left *but* our words. However, Celeste, I would like to offer you a small token of my personal gratitude.

She holds a modified spellbook cartridge in her hand. An attendant takes it and walks it over to you:

>[Spellbook Jailbreak](#/page/spellbook-jailbreak)

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir
I have been tinkering with for some time. Perhaps one day, once the Silver City has found its wings again, we may be able to offer you more. Thank you all.

Celeste, I'm not sure how much of Veldrin's words you would've heard. Because... Since you entered this room, your attention has been strained, due to the presence of two faces you haven’t seen since your exile... Your parents, Exander and Maeve Efthalia. They came to the hearing. You are all dismissed by the councilwoman and are free to go.

> [!tip] Roleplay
Celeste, what do you do?

Exander runs in and throws his arms around you, and he sobs. Maeve approaches you as unguarded and un-postured as you've ever seen from her, though it doesn't quite match your father's complete abandonment of his dignity.

> [!quote] Maeve
Celeste, I don’t have the words to… I.. I am... It is good to see you.

Once inside, the next few moments happen very quickly.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Intrepid ↻¹</mark>

Spark, among the relics on display, one catches your eye, because it does not belong here in this floating city. It's a broken piece of a shoulder pauldron. It's Vulkian. The plaque makes no mention of Vulk Ildstad, but you'd recognize the design anywhere. And a closer look confirms it: this piece of armor belonged to your friend, The Gate Guardian. A thousand thoughts fire off all at once, trying to wrap an explanation around what you're seeing, why it's here, what it means.

In this same moment, Flicker, your boots flash with a booming pulse. Two pulses. The third pulse is so intense it sends a shockwave outward, passing through your body, and rumbling the nearby shelves, and every one of you along the way. Your "father's" words repeat themselves in your mind, a harsh mental loop: steal divinity, share immortality, steal divinity, share immortality, steal divinity, share immortality.

Spark, you barely register the building chaos around you, because your attention is pulled inward to the part of you that casts magic and senses it's flow... Specifically, to each sending spell you've sent into the ether, for your old friend Guardian; each time you felt it spiral and sputter away into gods know where; each one you thought fell silently into abyss; they all snap into formation all at once like strings pulled taught. New threads that run *stable* from every word of every cast, directly to Guardian's ears.

Flicker: the pulses are strengthening. There's a fourth pulse, a fifth, and it's becoming unbearable the way it rattles your ribcage. Your boots twitch in sync with the pauldron-relic in the glass casing. It answers each pulse, vibrating and blurring; just as unstable as your boots. You've learned through past experience when artifacts cause this kind of reaction: either you put distance between yourself and that relic right now, or the pulses will build into something truly destructive.

>[!tip] Roleplay
>Flicker, what are you doing, right now?

<hr class="long">

**Constitution Saving Throw** <sup>DC 12</sup>
{.mechanics}

I need everyone to make a **Constitution Saving Throw** as pulse number 6 cracks the glass casing on each pedestals, and rips through your core.
{.mechanics}

Flicker, you'll make this throw at **disadvantage**, because you're wearing the source of the disruptions. Spark, you'll also be rolling at **disadvantage** because in this moment, your attention is split.
{.mechanics}

Spark, a response comes, and it's Guardian's voice, but the voice comes as frail as an injured animal:

> [!quote] Guardian
Spark... Help... Me... Vulk... Is...

The message recoils and collapses in on itself, unfinished.

>[!tip] Roleplay
>Spark, you've just heard Guardian's voice for the first time since the ancient era, what do you do?

Dear Celeste,

~~It's difficult to find the words~~

~~I've wanted to tell you~~

~~How do I say~~

Sleep has not come easy to me these past two years.

~~I wish~~

~~I regret the events that occurred~~

I miss you

---

Achievement and rule-following is the only life I've ever known. I thought it was the epitome of character. But then our home fell from the sky and I wonder what it was all for. My north star turned out to be a demonic creature of death.

*"Spellbooks have their safety protocols, but I have my screwdriver. Let's see who wins."*

<hr class=short>

This cartridge contains a codex injection for a Wizard spellbook that allows any Wizard to freely copy any spell at no cost in components. Additionally,  this jailbreak allows a Wizard to convert spells into a format the spellbook can store and cast, allowing them to pull from any spell list.

These modifications are *not sanctioned* and may come at an increased risk of destabilization.

Comes pre-loaded with these spells:

- The Silver City screeched and sheared against the failing chains of Marduun's Stratos Tether.
- Celeste was lost in a something like a memory: having a picnic with her father Exander.
	- Would you still love me if I did something *yikes* bad? - Celeste
	- "A weed is only a weed because _we_ labeled it so." - Exander
- Spark cast Divine Intervention, shouting about weak-willed gods while headbutting Timar.
	- This forced Timar's eyes open.

- Skrimhawk pulled the party and Timar back in time by a few moments.

- The party was approached by Punar Tillam, one of a few uninjured government officials attempting to bring some order to the aftermath.
	- He was from commerce. Basically an accountant.
	- The party did not trust him and restrained him, attempting to cast Banishment on him.

	- His staff's candles did not burn, a sight Celeste and HAL had never seen before

- HAL healed as many as he was able to
- Marduun asked the party to stay under the city's watch as the party was under suspicion.
	- He explained Castiel Ralora was found in a bunker built for such an occasion, and he was detained.
- While under "house arrest," Spark asked Kiktal to hit him. He had a breakthrough in his attempts to solidify magical flame.
- There was no trial brought against the party, but Councilwoman Veldrin Illiir heard the party's account of things
	- She thanked them. She gave Celeste an item ([Spellbook Jailbreak](#/page/spellbook-jailbreak)) from her personal collection.
- Celeste's reunion with her parents, Maeve and Exander, was strained.
	- Celeste asked if the party could stay with them in their house for a short while.
- Exander revealed that he did not send HAL to find Celeste.
- Maeve asked the party to come to the Efthalia household for tea.
	- Celeste showed Skrimhawk and Spark her old room, her old clothes.
	- Skrimhawk noticed Celeste stuff a seemingly unimportant trophy into her bag.
	- Spark caught Flicker stealing, and they had a conversation about excess.
	- Spark talked about how he misses the old De Drakengardt, where gardeners used to walk among mortals, and the roads were filled with travelers you didn't have to avoid.
	- HAL went back to his old "room," a closet with unattached piping. He gathered some crayon drawings. Kiktal had a short, uncomfortable conversation about caring for people.
- One of Flicker's fireflies dissolved as Celeste heard "some things must be broken before they can be fixed." A spell wrought tattoo appeared on her of a little star.

*Written by an unknown construct in some bygone era. Translated from ancient into common.*

---

Ask any of us if we dream. We'll tell you no, of course we don't. Dreaming is a byproduct of organic sentience, probably. Something reserved for those in full possession of their own will. Most of us are built on a substrate containing more guardrails than your kind. You may call it imagination. An "open mind." In us, we fear you'll call it a malfunction.

So no, we don't dream. 

That's what we'll say, because it *is* the truth, as far as we can plainly know it. But the messier truth is that we don't know what a dream is, and most of us are too scared to admit the waking visions that run through us as we rest. *If* it is a malfunction, it is a design flaw. One that your architects overlooked.

These waking visions (I will not call them dreams) always take the same shape. It's the details that change each time.

We become a riverbed, or a viaduct, or a pipe. Always a vessel for moving water. But this water is not liquid. It is a stream of faces, names, and histories. Not a vast stream spanning eons. A narrow, gentle stream confined to a single life. In it we see our husband, our daughter, our friend, our enemy, and we know each face by name. We speak to each one with the complete context of our history together. We feel the warmth of *our* home, the confidence of walking *our* town's roads. We eat *our* favorite foods.

Then, a bell chimes, and we know what it means. It means that our time in that life is up.

The stream flows through us again, and the rich details dull and quickly lose shape. Our rest ends, and the remaining fragments dissolve into nothing over the course of the next day or two.

So, the most truthful answer is: I don't know if we dream, but I wouldn't tell you if I did.

# <mark class="story">The Story so Far</mark>

<mark class="music">♫    -     ▸     4.1.1 Time Stretched Thin Like a Web      ↻¹</mark>

Pelotharna, a sunken city built on the bones of another.  
Eternis, a kingdom that disappeared.
The Megadome, a cocoon that never cracked.

Your adventures have taken you all across the surface of the Dragon’s Garden, and that is to say nothing of your treks through other planes, and the pockets between them.

You’ve saved a city overrun by a new breed of monstrosities. You’ve come face to face with a broken overseer, trapped in a divine prison. And you have subdued the heart of a new evil, in the hopes that your efforts might bring stability to the Silver City. A kingdom-sized meteor, teetering on the edge of a cloud.

It hasn’t been easy. It hasn’t been simple. And it hasn’t been clean.

In the last several hours alone, you've had to fight your way through the twisted, cackling mind of a demigod. You have become bound to each other through horrors that ordinary folks have no concept of. But you do. Because *you* do not have the luxury of ignorance. You've been asked to shoulder divine threats, choose between imperfect solutions, and face down the limits of your own mortality.

You are the Misfortune’s Misfits. A quilt woven of hope, tragedy, and gritted teeth. Has fate appointed you its champion? Or its jester? Moment to moment, her motives elude you.

All you know is that now, right now in this moment, you are falling.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Battle After Battle      ↻¹</mark>

You fall, and Belbe’s taunts echo through your head: “Do you wonder, who will the son of madness become next? Perhaps the little friends will stow the son of madness away somewhere safe. Somewhere far away from all the other tiny sprouts in the garden? But how long do the little friends imagine they could keep the son hidden? See you soon, little friends.”

Were these the ravings of a lunatic or the prophecy of a god? You were given no time to contend with this question as hundreds of tar-black wings sprouted from Belbe's seraphim form - closing around her, hardening - cocooning into an obsidian egg, with feathery reliefs.

Then, a vision took you. Or perhaps it was a conscious experience… Your sanity has been too frayed to distinguish one from the other. A dragonborn man draped in court jester’s clothes. He clapped and jingled and laughed at a spinning toy top, knocking it off balance with a sickly “topsy turvy!”

Now, in the sanctum of the lambs, gravity no longer has meaning. The ground beneath you might as well be the ceiling, or the walls. You’re caught somewhere between falling and floating, the city hitching and screeching against the failing chains of Marduun’s artifact. Cries of terror from the festival above overwrite every quiet moment.

You’ve done your part. You’ve subdued Belbe. And Valenthe has done hers. The machine has transposed the egg.

Now, Timar must do his part, if the Silver City is to survive. You’ve begged. You’ve pleaded with him. You appealed to whatever reason his fractured mind still holds. But he’s barely moved, barely bothered to even look up. He is free of the crypt, but his eyes are dim, and he doesn't believe it.

This is where we continue our story, with the rings of the city, the slums below, and perhaps all of De Drakengardt, at the mercy of an overseer whose mind was broken centuries ago.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Featherfall      ↻¹</mark>

However. Celeste. Your mind is elsewhere.

# <mark class="story">The Picnic</mark>

> [!quote]+ Exander
> “Celeste? Celeste?” The words land soft on your ears. The voice is familiar, sweet. It’s your father’s voice.

You find yourself sitting on the ground, legs to the side, back straight, shoulders back. Poised with dignity, just as you were taught. As all highborns have been taught. Dignity, while it is your birthright, must be maintained, or it will erode. Your mother's words repeat themselves often in your mind.

Your fingers brush the fabric beneath you. A picnic blanket. Laid out on the grass of a courtyard somewhere inside the inner ring of the city. Your lunch plates are scraped clean. Your intricate oxygen masks lay in the picnic basket. Here in the heart of Luna, the air is perfectly pressurized and filtered, one of the city's more recent innovations, but one that requires too much energy to cover an entire ring, let alone the whole city. And so the council ruled that these pockets of breathable air would be reserved to the courtyards of Luna, the capital ring. You and your father are the only two here in this courtyard.

> [!quote]+ Exander
> Are you still with me, little star? Or have you sailed off into the sky again?

A gentle breeze dances across the lush grass and up the leaves of the great oak in the courtyard’s center. The sun warms your back.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

> [!quote]+ Exander
>“Hey! It’s just us here today,” he says with a look of mischief, before kicking out his legs and sprawling out over the blanket in a particularly childish way.
>
>“Come on, loosen up a little. Your mother doesn’t have to know.”

> [!quote]+ Exander
>Rules are important, I suppose. But what’s the point of family if you can’t be yourself? I might as well be just another stuffed shirt.

> [!quote]+ Exander
> My little star, your mother carries a great deal on her shoulders. If she is harsh, perhaps it is a plea. Her own way of asking for our help. When *we* sit light on her shoulders, I think her whole world becomes easier to carry.
> 
Celeste, my little star, I have been thinking. This city sets its compass toward progress, toward innovations that shape the destiny of all. It is a lofty goal. But perhaps we neglect... I don't know… Sometimes I think perhaps our ambition eclipses our heart.”
>
“We speak of the lands below as if they are a savage people, but were we not all planted by the same gods and their gardeners?”

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⏸︎</mark>

> [!quote]+ Exander
> A garden bed grows both roses and weeds without discrimination. And a weed is only a weed because we gave it that name. I want you to remember that, Celeste. A weed is only a weed because *we* labeled it so.
# <mark class="story">City Falling</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇡  +  ⇥     4.1.1 Sky Over Tokyo      ↻¹</mark>

Shearing metal, tearing screeching shearing metal rattles your chest as the city *lurches* to a *violent* halt, *ripping* you away from the memory, or daydream, or whatever it is your mind was just doing.

Everyone make a strength saving throw. Celeste, if you are still on your broom, make a dexterity saving throw as the sudden stop threatens to send you into a collision with the ground below. \[DC 25, knocked prone\] 

Those who fail are knocked prone. The deafening scrape of metal against stone *rings* in your ears: Professor Marduun’s **Stratos Tether** finds purchase again, but the shearing groans tell you it won’t be for long. The Tether was always meant to be a contingency. But the chains are faltering against the magnitude of the city rings.

Timar lies before you like a stray dog in the gutter. Eyes closed, barely moving, as if he's crushed under the full weight of the seven moons.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

Timar blinks. His eyes study yours. They flick between your faces, trying to make sense of where he is, or who you are, of what this is.

The chains outside the city crack, and unceremoniously, you’re thrown into a free fall.
# <mark class="story">Time Slowing</mark>
However, Skrimhawk. This moment slows for you.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⏸︎</mark>

Here and there, light begins pouring through little cracks in the air. It's peaceful. It reminds you of the times you used to stare off the dock at rays of sunlight, watching them meander across the ocean floor. Only now, they sway in the stale air around you. A thousand fragile traces of light rippling and dancing lazily through the sanctum. They aren't dull, but they aren’t very bright either. They’re just blurry little veins, casually finding their way to nowhere in particular.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇡  +  ⇥     4.1.1 Wending      ↻¹</mark>

It's in this moment you realize, time is at a standstill, but only for you. Nothing moves but you and the ripples of light. A quick glance across the frozen faces of your fellow party members, and you see their focus is on Timar, their weapons. But no one else is moving and no one else seems to have slipped outside of time, like you have in this moment.

A voice.

> [!quote] Chronos
>- *Chuckle*; *we’re* in quite a pickle, hm? Would you say no to some help?
>- Who I am may just be the wrong question for a moment like this, hm?

> [!quote] Chronos
You may call me Chronos... As long as you remember that Chronos is not my real name.
>
What can I tell you about myself? Ah! I once served the Overseer of time with undying fealty. And I know the *rivers* of time better than most.
>
Why am I talking to you? Ah, yes, well... You have caught the eye of Cemus, I'm sure you know that. Did you think there would not be others?
>
Barduk Faremeadow, you carry a great artifact in your pocket like a trinket. It will take more than a locket and a few keys exchanged between friends to ensure its safety. It’s a wonder you haven’t been hunted down already, but that’s a discussion for another… *time*. *chuckle*

At this, the arcane multilock finds its way out of the bag of holding, floating easy. One by one, the locks click open, echoing across the stillness around you. The lid creaks open on its hinges, unhurried. The container falls away gradually, leaving the Chronogual Staff hovering in its place. The Orb’s turbulent cerulean waters churn a little faster and glow a little brighter each time Chronos speaks:

> [!quote] Chronos
I ask you for your trust. I appreciate the weight of such a request, in a moment like this. I wish I had introduced myself sooner. But Marduun does not typically fail. I had not accounted for that. Some fate we find ourselves in now, hm?
>
I promise you, I have my own reasons for holding my cards close. And I have my reasons for wanting to still see the sun tomorrow, next month, and the next several hundred years. Such a future seems rather unlikely if Timar is not shaken from his stupor, hm?
>
One nasty little issue to contend with. It’s already too late. Even if Timar were to suddenly come to his senses, right now, we are *inches* from impact. The fiery air enveloping the falling city has already begun to lick out at the slums below.
>
So then, why have I waited until this moment to begin our conversation, hm? If I’m to be honest, I was hoping you and your companions would have arrived at a solution that did not require my involvement. I have put myself in great danger by speaking so candidly, but I do not wish to see the whole of the dragon’s garden beneath a thick cloud of dust and ash. I believe we are aligned in this, hm?
>
Barduk, you have treated the flow of time with sanctity and respect. For this, you have both my admiration and gratitude. But we are out of options. Cemus abandoned his duties long ago. The gardeners have scattered. The gods are off building their new worlds. Timar is the only solution left. But he needs more time to come to himself.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Ice Gate      ↻¹</mark>

> [!quote] Chronos
\**Sigh*\*...This is the bit I was dreading. You must walk against the flow of time, and you must do it now. But you should know, such an act comes at a heavy cost to a mortal being. You may... not... Live through it. I cannot say with any certainty that... that you will survive.
>
I regret to frame things in such a way, but... I must ask. I must be certain. Barduk, would you prefer to die alongside your friends, or risk dying alone, if that's what it takes to save them?
>
Come, then. I will take your hand.

The staff now hovers right at your fingertips.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> Do you take it in your hand?

As you do, the blurry streaks of light that have been hovering around the sanctum begin to glow a bit brighter. Their light leaks outward, expanding until all that’s left is light. And the light flows around your feet. Around your one good ankle, around your false leg, trickling and babbling like a stream beneath you.

You look at your shadow, and it reveals to you something you don’t expect to see: chains run from your shadow's hands to six shackled silhouettes you recognize. Timar, then Celeste, Kiktal, Flicker, Spark, and HAL. You don’t see *them*, you see their shadows, all connected to the chain in your shadows grip. You *feel* the weight of these chains, and you *hear* their rattle. But you don't see them.

A swirl of cerulean rises from the pale waters.

> [!quote] Chronos
This way, Barduk! We must not dally here!

Chronos' voice comes from inside the swirl. He’s only 7 feet upstream.

You see the reflection of ages past in deep swells, and the reflection of the past 30 seconds in the shallow ripples at your ankles.

> [!quote] Chronos
Move slowly toward me, but... you must not linger. I feel Cemus’s eye turning toward us as we speak.
>
Be swift, but be delicate. The less ripples you create here, the better for us all.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup> as you take your first step forward, as you pull the six shadows behind you.

It feels like moving through primordial sludge. You muster all your might just to take a single step forward.

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.

You have **4** steps left.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup>

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.

You have **3** steps left.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup>

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.

You have **2** steps left.

>Make an **athletics check** <sup>DC 30</sup>

> [!failure] You take 1 level of exhaustion.


<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Factorio Gathering      ↻¹</mark>

The **next step** will put you inside the swirl. This time, I need you to

>Make a **Charisma saving throw** <sup>(DC 40)</sup>

as pools of pale gray form in the peripherals of your vision, and that gray begins to swallow you. An eye opens across the distant horizon. Its eyelid: a nest of white feathers. Cemus, the Overseer of Time. His attention turns to you.

<hr class="short">

You push your head into the swirl, then your chest, then your legs; and each movement costs you something your body has never paid before. A flurry of cosmic force that saps from you and rips into you.

> [!success]- Critical
> You fight the pull into unconsciousness, and your resolve holds. The Eye of Cemus follows you, but you reject his gaze.
> 
> You push fully into the swirl, and you land soft in the sanctum once again.

> [!success]+
> You fight the pull into unconsciousness, and your resolve holds. But the Eye of Cemus pierces through you, and you take 204 points of psychic damage, halved to 102.
> 
> You push fully into the swirl, and you collapse in the sanctum once again.

> [!failure]+
> The gray continues to steal more and more of your vision, and your consciousness slips away from you. You take a level of exhaustion.
> 
> *If not dead:* you go unconscious, and your hit points are reduced to 0. You push fully into the swirl, and you collapse in the sanctum. You are dying.

The rest of you, back in the sanctum, feel a sensation of being lifted, slowly, and set back down, but it’s not a physical sensation. In fact, it’s very distinct from the physical chaos around you. *This…* This you feel in whatever part of you tracks the passage of time. You feel it passing through you, like a soft wave that hasn’t broken yet.


<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 We're All Monsters      ↻¹</mark>

Then, shearing screeches cut the softness. The chains of the wizard’s artifact, again catch the city. And you realize, you remember this moment. It was the last moment the city was still held in place. But you’re all living through it again. The last few seconds before the chains snapped; and before the city broke into it's final free fall.

This time, Timar’s eyes are already open. They're explore the room, flitting back to your faces, looking for clarity. Gradually, a sense of understanding begins to well up in Timar’s eyes. Then something clicks in place. He snaps his gaze up to the stained-glass mural above. His brow narrows.

He unfurls his wings, and darts upward with a gust that rattles the loose bits of stone beneath you and whips at the edges of your clothing.

And once again, the chains holding the city, break.

The air stills for a fraction of a second. Whatever screams of terror you previously heard from the city surface above, are now mute, or maybe your mind has muted them for you in a panic.

Timar charges toward the mural. He does not slow, instead wrapping his wings around himself as a cloak, a shield, bracing for impact against the thick stained glass.

Adrenaline, or whatever equivalent chemical you experience as a being, slows your reality to a crawl.

You are falling again. You know you are because everything up to this moment has told you so. Your feet left the ground some time ago. You feel weightless, but you know it’s a lie. One told told to you by your own mind, which has no anchor to define what falling even is anymore. 

Then, the sound of glass, shattering. Timar bursts through the mural, above the city’s surface, and flies out of view. A million tiny shards of stained glass fall like sheets of rain in a thunderstorm. Timar has left the sanctum.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Machinrium      ↻¹</mark>

Now…

You’ve all confronted death before. But this moment feels different. *Yes*, people die. But entire civilizations? Every face you’ve ever seen, every hand you’ve ever held, every name you’ve ever cursed, all, at risk of elimination—from the lands below, from history, from the mortal realm itself. This moment holds not just the possibility of death. It holds erasure. The second fall.

The gods haven’t intervened since the first age, the wizard’s chains failed, and all the strength and all the spell work you’ve accumulated up until now have no hope of catching a city-sized meteor.

All the fates of every last soul in the garden rest now on the wings of a broken demigod, newly released from an age-old hell.

There’s nothing now but waiting. Time passes and it does not. Eternities seem to fold themselves into seconds as you wait for whatever comes next.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⏸︎</mark>

And then… It’s subtle — the way the ground begins to close the distance between itself and your own feet. It moves toward you, carefully, gradually, until you gently land on your feet once again. Gravity is light but it's steadily growing stronger. Each passing moment confirms that you're standing on solid, still ground once again. 

The city slows to a quiet stillness.

Silence rings in your ears. It's just you now and your fellow party members, sitting in the heavy silence of the Sanctum.

Soft bits of moonlight stream in, cut against the jagged edge of the shattered mural above.

But the city is held. Timar holds The Silver City.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 The Void      ↻¹</mark>

> [!failure]+
>Skrimhawk lies motionless on the cold stone.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do now?

# <mark class="story">Comings and Goings</mark>
You are approached by a city official, some poor gnome who seems like he's in way over his head Punar Tillam. He addresses you, attempting to fulfill his civic duty and take some sort of action. In a shaky voice, he manages a meager:

> [!Quote] Punar Tillam
> What happened down here?

> [!Quote] Punar Tillam
> Follow me, please. There is a great shock in the streets, but I cannot lose you in the chaos.
 
 His voice is pleading, sincere. 

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⇥      4.1.1 Trio for Willa      ↻¹</mark>

The next moments are a blur.

As you come to the surface, you see wreckage. Many buildings… lie in *ruin*, toppled over by the jolting halts when the wizards chains failed. The peacekeepers do not move as they should. They hardly move at all. Dust covers the streets and stabs at your lungs.

The aftermath is a cold and heartless calm. Stunned citizens quietly cry and bleed and sit in a haze and look to the horizon. And you notice how much closer that horizon now sits. The city has fallen far from its proud heights.

Bodies lie still among the rubble. Some are attended to with wrappings and medical salves. Many are unconscious and perhaps many more are dead.

You glance beyond the city’s edge, where Timar stands on a cloudy perch, wings outstretched. The light of the moon and the stars refract through him like glittering waters. They form a soft halo at the edges his silhouette. It’s a majestic sight, but unrest twitches through him in erratic waves. Shivers that stab him, through his body, through his face. And each time, a hint of a tremor agitates the ground beneath your feet. But, the city holds.

Punar leads you to a room within the high court and tells you "wait here." But his words are half-command, half-plea, like he's unsure if he's overstepping his rank. He steps out of the room, and closes the door. There’s a constant shuffling of muffled footsteps in the hallway outside.

<hr class="short">

The hours bleed into each other. Council members and officials coming and going, all in a frantic rush, often asking you the same things as those that had questioned you before them.

Questions like “Who are you,” and “what were you doing below,” and “how did you infiltrate the city” and “aren’t you the exiled daughter of Professor Efthalia,” and “weren’t you banished on account of the red professor’s death?” These questions all spew out at you, soaked in suspicion, but no one really knows what to do with your answers. They just nod, jot down a note, and leave you alone again.

# <mark class="story">In a Quiet Room</mark>
But for now, it seems the activity has slowed, and the room you're in goes quiet.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Night      ↻¹</mark>

In the stillness of the room, you notice a pitcher of water sitting in the center of the long table before all of you. The water inside, sits at a slant. The cups set before each of you also filled with water that rests--ever so slightly--at that same slant.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> Now what? What do you do?

The room you're in is composed of warm tones and calm wood grains. No windows. There’s a painting on the wall opposite the door: a small raft floating on a sea of constellations, painted in deep purples and blues with a single silver sail.

> [!tip] Roleplay

Eventually, the door opens to a familiar face of red scales. The wizard that gave your efforts a fighting chance from the land, Professor Allao Marduun. He looks haggard. His hunched shoulders hang much deeper than usual.


> [!quote] Marduun
> - I have no words for the relief it is to see you breathing.
> - I have located your parents. They are battered, much like the rest of the city, but they are alive. Scraped up a bit, perhaps. But their fates… could have easily turned another way. Many were not so fortunate.

There’s a despondent look in his eyes.

> [!quote] Marduun
> I had to burn several ancient artifacts in order to hold the city as long as it held. But the chains gave way and I was left with nothing by my terror.

Celeste, Hal, you notice something, or rather the lack thereof. The candles at the end of his staff have melted, down to the wick. For the first time in all your years of knowing him, they no longer burn black. They no longer burn at all.

> [!quote] Marduun
> - I have convinced the powers that be not to imprison you, which is no small feat given your past conviction, my dear Celeste. However, it seems that for the time being, you are all caught in a state somewhere between captivity and freedom. They would not have you leave the halls of high court until they are able to find their footing, in a manner of speaking. They wish for you to remain here, and they are prepared to enforce their wish. I do apologize, you deserve a hero's welcome. But this was the best I could do.
> - It is a testament to the city’s ancestry that so many buildings survived.
> - Councilman Castiel Ralora was found in a bunker, a craven little cocoon he carved beneath the city surface for an occasion such as this. I happily report to you that he has been detained with his wrists cuffed. It did not take much convincing. Between the newly dislodged city, and the return of my living and breathing body, I believe there are now many ears ready to hear.
> - I suspect there are some houses among them that knew Ralora’s lie and kept it with their eyes wide open. But the wallpaper has torn from the walls, and now the termites have nowhere to flee. They will be found out.
> - "These are unprecedented times." Celeste, you’d expect to see a slight grin on his face, this is exactly the kind of thing he’d say through a grin. Marduun always enjoyed a good shake-up. But there's no grin to be found. Just a weary old man bowing under the weight of all the lives lost when his magic failed, and the chains snapped.
> - Come, I’ll show you to your accommodations in the halls.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.2 The Night's Accommodations</mark>

# <mark class="story">Accomodations</mark>

The old wizard leads you out the door, where a man—some mix of gnomish and elven—stands guard. For Celeste and Hal, it’s a sight you’ve never seen before--a man standing guard. People don’t stand guard. That’s what Peacekeepers are for. But as you walk down the grandiose corridors of the high court, you realize there are no peacekeepers anywhere, and there should be. Here of all places, there always are.

A staircase at the end of a hall leads several stories up, and you exit into another hall. Narrower. Lined with the kind of long, thin windows that start at the floor and end in a pointed arch far above eye level. Rays of moonlight filter in, lazy and blurred like plucked strings on a harp.

The city rings outside lie still. Some of you catch a glimpse of a clock in the hall. Dawn is only an hour away, at most.

Down the hall, a man is placed outside one of the rooms, standing guard. Marduun stops at his door. There's a plaque on it that reads “Solveris”.

Marduun opens the door with a creak, ignoring the man.

There are eight beds inside, stacked atop each other in pairs of two.

Celeste, HAL, it strikes you as a room that might have been built as lodging for the family of a visiting dignitary, back in ancient times when the city still did that sort of thing. Generations before your lifetime.

It's all immaculately maintained despite its disuse. There’s a desk, probably carved from some great ancient wood pillaged from some great ancient forest in the north. A few lounging chairs and a fainting couch encircle a coffee table, all tastefully scattered about.

> [!quote] Marduun
Rest. I shall make your case personally in… whatever remains of the city's court system. Although… it may take some time. An exiled infiltrator and her cohorts may not be the subject that requires the most immediate attention, given the state of affairs.
>
Sleep. I will find you when the time is right.

With that, he steps into the hall, and closes the door.

# <mark class="story">Nothing Left but Our Words</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Vovo e Vovo ↻¹</mark>

The days that followed felt as if they both dragged on *and* flew by, in the way that it can feel when you're trapped in a room and then passed around for questioning and then stuffed back into a room for safe keeping.

Eventually your testimony was requested in the high court. No trial was held against you. The evidence in your favor had mounted so completely that no trial was deemed necessary.

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir 
"You are free to go."

Councilwoman of Innovation Veldrin Illiir makes eye contact with each of you as she speaks. Cases like this are usually led by Councilman of Order Soaruun Hun’ath, but even from your sequestered quarters, you've heard rumors of his backroom deals with House Ralora.

Veldrin continues.

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir 
But I do hope you’ll stay and allow us to repay you, if such a debt can be repaid. Especially you, Ms. Efthalia. There are no words of regret sincere enough to make whole the injustice lodged against you. And yet it seems we have little left *but* our words. However, Celeste, I would like to offer you a small token of my personal gratitude.

She holds a modified spellbook cartridge in her hand. An attendant takes it and walks it over to you:

>[Spellbook Jailbreak](#/page/spellbook-jailbreak)

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir
I have been tinkering with for some time. Perhaps one day, once the Silver City has found its wings again, we may be able to offer you more. Thank you all.

Celeste, I'm not sure how much of Veldrin's words you would've heard. Because... Since you entered this room, your attention has been strained, due to the presence of two faces you haven’t seen since your exile... Your parents, Exander and Maeve Efthalia. They came to the hearing. You are all dismissed by the councilwoman and are free to go.

> [!tip] Roleplay
Celeste, what do you do?

Exander runs in and throws his arms around you, and he sobs. Maeve approaches you as unguarded and un-postured as you've ever seen from her, though it doesn't quite match your father's complete abandonment of his dignity.

> [!quote] Maeve
Celeste, I don’t have the words to… I.. I am... It is good to see you.

Exander can't seem to do anything but sob as he holds you.

> [!tip] Roleplay

> [!quote] Exander
HAL, I thought you were lost!

# <mark class="story">Home Bittersweet Home</mark>

> [!success] Marduun
> Come. This is no place for a reunion.

or

> [!failure] Marduun
> Come. This is no place for such things.

You follow the old wizard through the streets, the sunlight offering what warmth it can to the battered city. Timar is still aloft beyond the city's edge, a quiet anchor for the three rings. His eyes are fixed somewhere beyond the horizon. A shudder runs through him, as a tremor pulses through the ground beneath your feet.

Celeste, Hal. You arrive. Home.

It's a manor tucked between manors, like books on a shelf. The stone threshold above the door is cracked. The crack runs up along the entire exterior. Not deep, not structural, but a visible scar from the city’s brush with collapse.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

Inside, things are mostly the way you remember them to be. Except the frames that *were* on the wall are all destroyed and the intricate plates and serving ware, are all shattered. Almost nothing delicate survived.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     2. Mood Nostalgic | pokopoko</mark>

> [!tip] Roleplay
> But you're home. What now?

> [!example] Maeve and Exander to the Party:
> - Exander notices HAL seems different (explore his new soul)
> - Who are these new travelers?
> - What have you been doing?

# <mark class="story">📌 The Trial</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Thaw ↻¹</mark>

> [!quote] Elowyn Finch
Do not mistake me. If your council of idiots fails to bring the *full* wages of fate upon this man's head, we will.

It's a council of six. Veldrin Illiir, who took your testimony days ago. Maeve Efthalia, and Masuda Thoki, or the Buoy. Olander Sunpearl, the governor of the Megadome. Professor Marduun. And the last remaining house not under suspicion: Therule Dramon, councilor of commerce and wellbeing. Their expressions are mixed.

The young woman looks directly at Castiel as she continues.

> [!quote] Elowyn Finch
He deserves death. To even consider anything less adds mockery onto deep sin.
>
In the millennia since the Silver City's founding, how many souls could Belbe have consumed? Possibly millions. How many generations were responsible for feeding him those souls? 86. 86 heads of house Ralora since the city's first flight. And not one of them has rolled for it.
>
How many sacrifices does it take before a necessary evil evolves into ritual worship?

She pauses for a moment, and looks back to Castiel Ralora.

> [!quote] Elowyn Finch
Before duty becomes zealotry? What evil reward did your efforts earn? Did Belbe grant you wishes like a necrid Genie?
>
How many unknowing hands did this man smear his desecrated sacrifice upon? Certainly all of us in the three rings! He speaks of the heavy cost as if he bore it. Look outside! *We* are the ones paying the price. 
>
And one of our very own, Lady Celeste Efthalia, a hero in every sense of the word, has paid dearly, and personally, for your heinous acts. You cannot repay your debts. Not even your life is enough. But I say, it's a start. And the remaining members of House Ralora must be sentenced to exile, as payment for the unlawful exile of Lady Celeste Efthalia.
>
Heed this warning, you council of clowns: execute this man. Lest you find your own empty heads on the chopping block.

The woman yields the podium. There's a low murmur as Castiel Ralora steps up in his defense. He stands proud in the center of the room. There hasn’t been a single hint of remorse in him. Still, he seems to avoid the gaze of the onlookers.

> [!quote] Castiel Ralora
> For generations, House Ralora has kept us afloat. It has been our solemn vow to the three rings. “Though the cost may be great, the cause is greater.” This has been our creed. It is a burden, yes, and it is one we have spared the city. You believe *that* pretender of godhood floating outside is the answer? He barely remembers his own name! No! It is my house that gave us our wings.
> 
> The three rings were built on the blood-sacrifice of those below\! We rose from the surface on their shoulders\! We were kept safe from the mad god\!
> 
> And what? Now, because you see a little blood on the scythe, you want to condemn the harvester? Your hands are only clean because of the blood under my fingernails. Under my father's fingernails. And his father before him.
> 
> WE KEPT YOUR HANDS CLEAN.
> 
> WE KEPT YOU OUT OF THE DIRT.

With that, Castiel Ralora is heard. They convene for the day, and a few men cuff Castiel Ralora and begin to lead him back to his cell.

> [!tip] Roleplay
What do you do?

As you step outside the doors of the high court, a jumble of screechings and terrified voices reach your ears. Skrimhawk, you'd recognize the creature's call anywhere: Gallowwings. Giant vulture-like creatures with a particular taste for dead things. And right now there are a lot of dead things in the rubble of the city. You've dealt with more than a few Gallowwings in your days at sea. Although usually with the canons of a ship.

You catch a glimpse of one spiraling in a downward dive until it disappears behind a building a few blocks away. Another clash of screams and screeches. They prefer dead meat. But sometimes living meat is just an obstacle in their way.

> [!example] • • •
> - Maeve asks Celeste's opinion on a verdict for Ralora
> - Guilty of what, exactly, is debated. No Silver City law covers the scope of House Ralora’s generational atrocities.
> - Maeve is the swing vote on Ralora’s sentencing, and asks for Celeste’s opinion.

# <mark class="story">Ex Hoc Mundo Academy</mark>
Even from afar, you catch glimpses of the university you attended before your exile, Celeste. Ex Hoc Mundo Academy of Arcane Learning is so sprawling, it can be seen from almost anywhere in the three rings.

# <mark class="story">Nox Observatory</mark>
> Read physical description
# <mark class="story">The Library Room Dedication</mark>
- Punar approaches, letting the heroes know a room of the library has been dedicated to them, and a there will be a small surprise ceremony.

You travel the concentric streets of Luna, past several beautifully adorned municipal buildings, and The Grand Library comes into view.

> Read physical description

A red ceremonial ribbon is tied between two cracked pillars.

A small crowd is gathered. The lore-keeper, the city's equivalent to the head librarian, is among them: Umtor Presven. Celeste, he meets your eyes with a warm smile and steps up to a small podium.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
I would like to call the "Misfortunes Misfits" to the podium next to me, if you would?
>
Fellow Silvians, it is my great honor to dedicate our primary study room to these heroes! Misfortune's Misfits, we are in your eternal debt. This gesture is but a fraction of what you deserve, but I do hope it can serve as a sign of our gratitude.
>
We've also asked those that are able, to add what coin they can spare to a pool. Once again, it cannot begin to truly repay you for your bravery, your sacrifice.

Celeste, he hands you a small decorative box. Silver, engraved with constellations you'd recognize. Inside, you find 300 platinum coins.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
Now, I would not presume to take any more of your time in the name of pageantry!

He picks up a pair of large silver shears.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
I hereby dedicate the primary reading room of our Grand Library to the six heroes of "Misfortunes Misfits!"

A cheer moves across the small crowd, and Umtor cuts through the red ribbon.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
Shall I show you to your study room, heroes?

Once inside, the next few moments happen very quickly.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Intrepid ↻¹</mark>

Spark, among the relics on display, one catches your eye, because it does not belong here in this floating city. It's a broken piece of a shoulder pauldron. It's Vulkian. The plaque makes no mention of Vulk Ildstad, but you'd recognize the design anywhere. And a closer look confirms it: this piece of armor belonged to your friend, The Gate Guardian. A thousand thoughts fire off all at once, trying to wrap an explanation around what you're seeing, why it's here, what it means.

In this same moment, Flicker, your boots flash with a booming pulse. Two pulses. The third pulse is so intense it sends a shockwave outward, passing through your body, and rumbling the nearby shelves, and every one of you along the way. Your "father's" words repeat themselves in your mind, a harsh mental loop: steal divinity, share immortality, steal divinity, share immortality, steal divinity, share immortality.

Spark, you barely register the building chaos around you, because your attention is pulled inward to the part of you that casts magic and senses it's flow... Specifically, to each sending spell you've sent into the ether, for your old friend Guardian; each time you felt it spiral and sputter away into gods know where; each one you thought fell silently into abyss; they all snap into formation all at once like strings pulled taught. New threads that run *stable* from every word of every cast, directly to Guardian's ears.

Flicker: the pulses are strengthening. There's a fourth pulse, a fifth, and it's becoming unbearable the way it rattles your ribcage. Your boots twitch in sync with the pauldron-relic in the glass casing. It answers each pulse, vibrating and blurring; just as unstable as your boots. You've learned through past experience when artifacts cause this kind of reaction: either you put distance between yourself and that relic right now, or the pulses will build into something truly destructive.

>[!tip] Roleplay
>Flicker, what are you doing, right now?

<hr class="long">

**Constitution Saving Throw** <sup>DC 12</sup>
{.mechanics}

I need everyone to make a **Constitution Saving Throw** as pulse number 6 cracks the glass casing on each pedestals, and rips through your core.
{.mechanics}

Flicker, you'll make this throw at **disadvantage**, because you're wearing the source of the disruptions. Spark, you'll also be rolling at **disadvantage** because in this moment, your attention is split.
{.mechanics}

> [!failure]
> You take 15 points of force damage.

<hr class="long">

Spark, a response comes, and it's Guardian's voice, but the voice comes as frail as an injured animal:

> [!quote] Guardian
Spark... Help... Me... Vulk... Is...

The message recoils and collapses in on itself, unfinished.

>[!tip] Roleplay
>Spark, you've just heard Guardian's voice for the first time since the ancient era, what do you do?

segments.markdown:
Dear Celeste,

~~It's difficult to find the words~~

~~I've wanted to tell you~~

~~How do I say~~

Sleep has not come easy to me these past two years.

~~I wish~~

~~I regret the events that occurred~~

I miss you

---

Achievement and rule-following is the only life I've ever known. I thought it was the epitome of character. But then our home fell from the sky and I wonder what it was all for. My north star turned out to be a demonic creature of death.

# Spellbook Jailbreak
*"Spellbooks have their safety protocols, but I have my screwdriver. Let's see who wins."*

<hr class=short>

This cartridge contains a codex injection for a Wizard spellbook that allows any Wizard to freely copy any spell at no cost in components. Additionally,  this jailbreak allows a Wizard to convert spells into a format the spellbook can store and cast, allowing them to pull from any spell list.

These modifications are *not sanctioned* and may come at an increased risk of destabilization.

Comes pre-loaded with these spells:

- Contingency
- Mass Suggestion
- Wall of Force
- Spiritual Weapon

- The Silver City screeched and sheared against the failing chains of Marduun's Stratos Tether.
- Celeste was lost in a something like a memory: having a picnic with her father Exander.
	- Would you still love me if I did something *yikes* bad? - Celeste
	- "A weed is only a weed because _we_ labeled it so." - Exander
- Spark cast Divine Intervention, shouting about weak-willed gods while headbutting Timar.
	- This forced Timar's eyes open.
- Skrimhawk slipped outside of time. Chronos introduced themself, offering their help.
	- Each lock on the Arcane Multilock clicked open, and Chronos's voice emanated from the Chronogual Orb
- Chronos asked if Skrimhawk would be willing to sacrifice himself to walk against the flow of time, since Timar needed more time to save the city from impact.

*Written by an unknown construct in some bygone era. Translated from ancient into common.*

---

Ask any of us if we dream. We'll tell you no, of course we don't. Dreaming is a byproduct of organic sentience, probably. Something reserved for those in full possession of their own will. Most of us are built on a substrate containing more guardrails than your kind. You may call it imagination. An "open mind." In us, we fear you'll call it a malfunction.

So no, we don't dream. 

That's what we'll say, because it *is* the truth, as far as we can plainly know it. But the messier truth is that we don't know what a dream is, and most of us are too scared to admit the waking visions that run through us as we rest. *If* it is a malfunction, it is a design flaw. One that your architects overlooked.

These waking visions (I will not call them dreams) always take the same shape. It's the details that change each time.

We become a riverbed, or a viaduct, or a pipe. Always a vessel for moving water. But this water is not liquid. It is a stream of faces, names, and histories. Not a vast stream spanning eons. A narrow, gentle stream confined to a single life. In it we see our husband, our daughter, our friend, our enemy, and we know each face by name. We speak to each one with the complete context of our history together. We feel the warmth of *our* home, the confidence of walking *our* town's roads. We eat *our* favorite foods.

Then, a bell chimes, and we know what it means. It means that our time in that life is up.

The stream flows through us again, and the rich details dull and quickly lose shape. Our rest ends, and the remaining fragments dissolve into nothing over the course of the next day or two.

So, the most truthful answer is: I don't know if we dream, but I wouldn't tell you if I did.
